name: Prize crossword No 25,238
preamble: Ten solutions have something in common; their clues lack a definition.

clue.text: Strange date ditched

indicators.note: something ditched is thrown away, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a five-letter synonym of strange, uncanny
D is the standard abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a date because it has turned odd.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no definition: this is one of the ten themed answers, all composers.
explanation.definitionFit: Judith Weir is a Scottish composer of operas and choral works, appointed Master of the Queen's Music in 2014.

clue.text: A friend he lost (I lost), executed naturally

indicators.note: a letter that is lost goes missing, so it is taken out of the fodder
letters that are lost have wandered off their route, so they come back in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone mourns a lost friend, who was put to death in a natural way.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(I lost)' is a separate instruction: remove one letter before rearranging, so the anagram fodder is seven letters plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing done freehand is produced without rulers or other instruments, by unaided natural skill.

clue.text: No time to drink up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the string runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the usual abbreviation for time
to sip is to drink

explanation.surface: A call that there is no time left for drinking up.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: this is one of the ten themed composers.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Piston was an American composer and Harvard teacher, known for symphonies and the ballet The Incredible Flutist.

clue.text: Doctor Richard Leakey's fossil hunters famously did in 1984

definitions.text: Richard Leakey's fossil hunters famously did in 1984

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for a surgeon or doctor

blocks.clueFragment: Richard Leakey's fossil hunters famously did in 1984
blocks.note: second meaning, read as two words: Leakey's team spotted the skeleton of Turkana Boy in 1984

explanation.surface: A doctor connected with Leakey's famous fossil discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as SAW BONES and it describes what Leakey's team did when they found the Turkana Boy skeleton in Kenya.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbones is old jocular slang for a surgeon, from the amputations once routine in the trade.

clue.text: Broadcast about sports body star

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
the LTA is the Lawn Tennis Association, British tennis's governing body

explanation.surface: A sports star being covered on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sports body star' reads as a famous athlete, but the last word stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila, one corner of the Summer Triangle.

clue.text: As carboxylic acid is lacy, top to bottom

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for an adjective-like chemical term

indicators.note: in a down entry the top letter is moved to the foot, rotating the word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry note likening an acid to delicate lace.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the L of LACY from first to last spells the chemical term.
explanation.definitionFit: An acyl group is the fragment left when a carboxylic acid loses its hydroxyl group, so such acids are acyl compounds.

clue.text: Northerner's age — or diet — has no bounds

indicators.note: with no boundaries the outer edges are gone, so the first and last letters drop away

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A northerner's lifestyle, whether age or diet, knows no limits.
explanation.walkthrough: Run AGE OR DIET together and strip its outer A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Geordie is a native of Tyneside, around Newcastle in north-east England, so a northerner.

clue.text: Say Evelyn said "Hank"

indicators.note: said means spoken, so it is the sound that counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: Evelyn Waugh the novelist, whose surname is pronounced like war
a hank of hair is a lock

explanation.surface: Evelyn is quoted calling someone Hank.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: one of the themed composers. 'Say' marks Evelyn as an example name, pointing to the novelist Waugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Warlock was the pen name of Philip Heseltine, an English composer of songs and the Capriol Suite.

clue.text: Having no master from the start, pro swallows back drink at far edge of green

definitions.text: Having no master from the start

indicators.note: back means backwards, so the word is read in reverse
to swallow is to take inside, so one piece goes into another
the far edge of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: to be pro something is to be for it
beer is a drink
the last letter of green

explanation.surface: A golf pro sinks a drink at the far side of the green.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs to 'from the start', which looks like a letter selection instruction but is part of the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone freeborn was born not a slave, so was never subject to any owner throughout life.

clue.text: Small sketch of Tom and Spike?

blocks.note: Tom Thumb, the tiny hero of folk tale
a spike is a large nail

explanation.surface: A little drawing of the cartoon cat Tom and the bulldog Spike.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom and Spike look like the Tom and Jerry cartoon characters; each name is completed or swapped for a word instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail sketch is a quick small drawing or brief outline, about the size of a thumbnail.

clue.text: Out of bed, possibly dreadlocked, so dressed down

blocks.note: out of bed is up
dreadlocks are one kind of braided hair, hence possibly

explanation.surface: Someone gets up, hair in dreadlocks, and throws on casual clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed down' suggests casual clothing, but here it means scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid someone is to scold them severely, the same as giving them a dressing-down.

clue.text: See 15
Chablis ousts tea on Sunday!

indicators.note: to oust is to throw out, so some letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written
cha is British slang for tea
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: A cheer for wine replacing tea on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: one of the themed composers. Take the tea off the front of the wine, then add the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Bliss was an English composer and Master of the Queen's Music, known for the film score Things to Come.

clue.text: Lean right and put out bust

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the word is rearranged

blocks.note: a plane or bike banks when it leans into a turn
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to lean to the right and put out a sculpted bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'out' alone works on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust is an informal word for bankrupt, as in a business that has gone bust.

clue.text: Catherine the Sixth (unknown)

blocks.note: Catherine Parr was the sixth wife of Henry VIII
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A queen whose identity is uncertain, styled like royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: one of the themed composers. 'The Sixth' looks like a regnal number but refers to Henry VIII's sixth wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Hubert Parry was an English composer best known for setting Blake's poem Jerusalem to music.

clue.text: Charlie, 1960s-style girl: underwear accepted

blocks.note: British slang for a young woman, at its height in the 1960s
a bra is an item of underwear
in means accepted or fashionable

explanation.surface: A swinging sixties girl named Charlie, whose underwear passes muster.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie looks like a name, but in British slang a charlie is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdbrain is a silly, empty-headed person, the same sense as calling someone a proper charlie.

clue.text: Miss going east of eastern tip of Shandong

indicators.note: with east to the right, the eastern tip of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: the last letter of Shandong
a miss is a girl or lass

explanation.surface: A young woman travelling to the far east of a Chinese province.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: one of the themed composers. In an across entry, east of means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Glass is an American minimalist composer, famous for operas such as Einstein on the Beach.

clue.text: "Side Wall" has old Hollywood heartthrob teamed with Close

blocks.note: Clark Gable, star of Gone with the Wind
a close is an end

explanation.surface: A film called Side Wall pairs a classic leading man with Glenn Close.
explanation.walkthrough: Close looks like the actress Glenn Close but is the plain noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gable end is the triangular-topped end wall of a pitched-roof building, forming its side.

clue.text: See 9
But beach bum is a water softener

indicators.note: bum is slang for bad or faulty, so the letters are in a poor arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beach bum, it turns out, softens hard water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beach bum' reads as a loafer, but 'bum' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath cube is a compressed block of salts dropped into the bath to soften and scent the water.

clue.text: Gave credit for publicity about writer

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: an ad is publicity
a scribe is a writer

explanation.surface: An author gets acknowledgement in some promotional material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' here is positional, not 'concerning': the publicity literally wraps round the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe something to someone is to attribute it to them, crediting them with it.

clue.text: Act like a pig, covering flipping lot with eggs

indicators.note: flipping can mean crazy or upset, so the letters get scrambled
a cover goes around something, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written
roe is fish eggs

explanation.surface: A greedy diner piles a whole plate high with eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive, but it turns the next word round.
explanation.definitionFit: To rootle is to dig about with the snout, as pigs do when foraging, a variant of root.

clue.text: Familiar state, yet unfamiliar

indicators.note: unfamiliar means strange, so the letters appear in an odd order

blocks.note: MA is the abbreviation for Massachusetts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A paradox: a condition that is known yet strange.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue opposes familiar and unfamiliar; one is the definition and the other the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Matey describes behaviour that is friendly and chummy, being on easy terms with someone.

clue.text: Big fish — both sides consumed by chief

indicators.note: what is consumed is taken inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: main means chief
right and left, R and L

explanation.surface: A big shot has eaten both halves of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big fish' sounds like an important person, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The marlin is a large ocean game fish with a long spear-like bill, prized by sport anglers.

clue.text: Dog hides tail after phosphorous feed

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
Rover is a stock name for a dog
the tail is the end

explanation.surface: A dog conceals its tail after being given chemical-laced food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places P in front, since the dog comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Provender is animal fodder such as hay or grain, or jocularly any food.

clue.text: Gin tipped over?

indicators.note: something tipped over is upside down, so in a down entry the word reads upwards

blocks.note: a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: Someone has knocked over the gin.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: one of the themed composers. Gin is the drink in the surface but an old word for a snare here.
explanation.definitionFit: Arvo Pärt is an Estonian composer of spare, bell-like sacred music such as Spiegel im Spiegel.

clue.text: Say Bill is rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the string runs backwards

blocks.note: eg, for example, means say
AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A proposed law has been voted down.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: one of the themed composers. Bill is an account, not a proposed law.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cage was an American avant-garde composer, notorious for 4'33", a piece of silent performance.

clue.text: Kelly, one of many passed on?

blocks.note: first meaning: the forename of the dancer Kelly of Singin' in the Rain
second meaning: a unit of heredity, one of thousands inherited

explanation.surface: A Kelly asks whether she is one of many who have died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed on' suggests death, but here it means inherited.
explanation.definitionFit: Genes are units of heredity handed down from parents to offspring, and each person carries thousands of them.

clue.text: Flanks of inferior antelope

indicators.note: flanks are the sides, so only the outside letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of inferior
the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: The sides of a poor-quality antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: one of the themed composers, not the country it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ireland was an English composer of songs, piano music and church anthems in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Performing is welcomed by the Bee Gees, family-wise

indicators.note: a guest who is welcomed is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the Bee Gees were the Gibb brothers, so as a family they are the Gibbs
a performer is on stage

explanation.surface: A performer is greeted by the Bee Gees, treated like one of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition: one of the themed composers; the apes are a false trail. Bee Gees were the brothers Gibb.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando Gibbons was an English Tudor and Jacobean composer of madrigals, keyboard pieces and church anthems.
